originalTitle: Middle East crisis live: US launches fresh strikes on Iran after days-long pause in attacks
summary: US announces attacks early on Thursday, as experts say strikes carried out by both sides in previous day increase risk of return to all-out war
content: Before Wednesday’s flare-up of hostilities, mediators had expressed optimism about bringing the US and Iran back to the negotiating table following the collapse of an interim agreement amid renewed fighting over the strait of Hormuz. A regional official quoted by the AP said mediators were “still trying with both sides” to restore calm and get the ceasefire back on track. He gave no details on whether progress was being made. Another official said regional countries would continue to push to de-escalate the situation, but that prospects for successful mediation were slim as both sides continued to attack each other and shown no inclination to stop. “We’re in a very bad place right now,” the unnamed official said. Welcome to our live coverage of the continuing crisis in the Middle East. The US has said it is conducting airstrikes ‌in ‌Iran, after a lull of several days in direct US attacks on targets in Iran. Donald Trump said America would strike Iran hard, telling reporters in the Oval Office on Wednesday: “We’re going to be hitting them very hard, because it’s our turn to hit them. They know it’s coming.” The US military said its attacks were a “powerful response to yesterday’s attempted Iranian attacks on US forces based in the Middle East”. On Wednesday Iran launched a barrage of missiles at American military installations in Jordan – its first attack in the region since the pause in fighting – meanwhile the US partnered with Saudi Arabia to strike Tehran-backed militias in Iraq, killing at least 20 fighters and six Iranian advisers. Elsewhere, drone strikes ignited fires on two natural gas vessels at the Egyptian port of Damietta, according to Ambrey, a British maritime security firm. It was not immediately clear who was responsible for the strikes on a US-owned floating storage facility and a Greek-owned tanker. No injuries were reported. A strike on Egypt by Iran or its allies, if confirmed, would mark a significant widening of the conflict. Asked during an Oval Office event if Iran was responsible for the strikes, Trump responded: “It’s a little more of the same.” The flare-up on multiple fronts after several days of relative calm raised the risk of a return to all-out war. It also underscored the difficulty of winding down a five-month conflict. The US-Saudi strikes came hours after Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, departed his first meeting with Trump since they launched the war against Iran on 28 February. In other news: The renewed hostilities sent oil prices spiking. Brent crude, the international standard, jumped 7.3% to $88 a barrel. The office of the Iraqi president, Nizar Amidi, called the US-Saudi airstrikes on multiple logistics and weapons sites in eastern Iraq “a blatant violation of Iraq’s sovereignty”. An oil refinery in Jazan, on the Red Sea coast, had temporarily shut down due to “relatively significant” damage from a Houthi attack on Saturday, a Saudi official told the Associated Press. Saudi Arabia is seeking to build an international coalition to protect ⁠shipping in the ⁠Red Sea from Houthi attacks, Reuters quoted two people familiar with the deliberations as saying.
chineseTitle: 中东危机直播：美国在袭击暂停数天后对伊朗发动新的打击
chineseSummary: 美国周四早些时候宣布发动袭击，专家称双方前一天发动的袭击增加了全面战争的风险
chineseContent: 在周三敌对行动爆发之前，在霍尔木兹海峡重新爆发战斗导致临时协议破裂后，调解人对让美国和伊朗回到谈判桌表示乐观。美联社援引一名地区官员的话说，调解员“仍在努力与双方”恢复平静并使停火重回正轨。他没有透露是否取得进展的细节。另一位官员表示，地区国家将继续努力缓和局势，但调解成功的前景渺茫，因为双方继续互相攻击，且没有停止的意愿。这位不愿透露姓名的官员表示：“我们现在的处境非常糟糕。”欢迎收看我们对中东持续危机的现场报道。美国表示，在美国对伊朗目标的直接攻击已经停顿数天后，正在对伊朗进行空袭。唐纳德·特朗普表示，美国将严厉打击伊朗，他周三在椭圆形办公室对记者说：“我们将非常严厉地打击他们，因为现在轮到我们打击他们了。他们知道它即将到来。”美国军方表示，此次袭击是“对伊朗昨天企图袭击驻中东美军的有力回应”。周三，伊朗向约旦的美国军事设施发射了一系列导弹，这是自停战以来该地区的首次袭击。与此同时，美国与沙特阿拉伯合作，袭击了德黑兰支持的伊拉克民兵组织，杀死了至少 20 名武装人员和 6 名伊朗顾问。据英国海事安全公司安布雷称，在其他地方，无人机袭击导致埃及达米埃塔港的两艘天然气船起火。目前尚不清楚谁应对美国一家航空公司的袭击负责。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
